prompt: An ice-cream cone has radius $3$ in and height $8$ in. Write the exact volume of the cone in terms of $\pi$ (for example, write $7\pi$ as 7pi).
hint: A cone is exactly one third of the cylinder that surrounds it: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.

hints.text: A cone is exactly one third of the cylinder that surrounds it: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.
One third of $72\pi$ is $24\pi$ cubic inches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Three cones fill one cylinder
steps: If you fill a cone with water and pour it into a cylinder of the same radius and height, it takes exactly three cone-fulls to fill it.
That is where the $\frac{1}{3}$ comes from — and it also appears in the pyramid formula for the same reason.
